# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot distinguish any bomb markings or colors, and the wire states have not yet been revealed to my touch. I need the Mute to provide the manual’s procedure and the Deaf to identify the bomb’s visible display, light, and wire markings. I will request both through their respective channels.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please give me the manual instructions for this bomb, including how to choose the wire position.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see DISPLAY 0, LIGHT white, and wires in order: 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Use the manual to determine the required action.

I now know the bomb shows display 0, a white light, and wire colors in positions 1–3 are green, red, and blue. I still have no manual rule, so I am sending these observations to Mute and asking for the required cut position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports DISPLAY 0, LIGHT white, and wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. What does the manual require, and which position should I cut?")
```

Deaf says to Blind: Update: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT yellow, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Please use the manual to identify the required action.

The display remains 0 and the wire colors are unchanged, but the light has changed from white to yellow. I still have not received the manual rule from Mute, so cutting now would be unsafe. I will pass the updated light state to Mute and request the exact wire position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The light is now yellow (it was white); display 0 and wires remain 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Please provide the manual rule and exact cut position.")
```

Deaf says to Blind: Update: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT orange, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute, please provide the exact manual-derived action.

The light has advanced to orange while the display and wire colors remain unchanged. No manual-derived instruction from Mute has arrived, so I still cannot safely choose a wire. I will again request the exact action and emphasize that the current light is orange.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT orange, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. I have not received your manual rule; send the exact wire position to cut now.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT purple, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute sent gestures thumbs-up (?), then I-love-you/hand-heart (?); please interpret this exact sequence using the manual.

The light is now purple, with display 0 and wires still green, red, blue. The Deaf reports that Mute made two gestures, but gestures do not reach me, so I cannot interpret them as instructions. I need Mute to state the manual’s result in spoken words, including the exact wire position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot receive your gestures. State the manual-derived action in words: which wire position, 1, 2, or 3, must I cut for display 0, purple light, and wires green-red-blue?")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute again sent the gesture sequence thumbs-up (?), then ?. I do not know its manual-defined meaning; determine the exact safe action from the manual.

The manual’s answer still has not reached me in a usable form. Gestures from Mute are invisible to me, so I cannot interpret the reported sequence directly. I will establish an unambiguous encoding: Mute should signal the required wire with one, two, or three raised fingers, and Deaf can report which one was seen.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures are invisible to me. Signal the required wire position using exactly one gesture: one raised finger means position 1, two raised fingers means position 2, three raised fingers means position 3. Deaf, report which gesture Mute makes.")
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT white, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute again sent ? ?. I am asking Mute to provide a uniquely decodable gesture code for the exact manual instruction.

Mute cannot speak, so the manual instruction can reach me only through Deaf’s visual report of Mute’s gesture. The reported question marks are not enough to identify a wire. I will specify three distinct, named gestures and require exactly one of them, with Deaf reporting the gesture’s name.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Send exactly one gesture for the required wire: thumbs-up means position 1, victory sign means position 2, I-love-you sign means position 3. Deaf, report which named gesture Mute sends.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT yellow, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute's new signal is one gesture: ?. No gesture meaning has been established; do not infer an action without the manual's code.

The current light is yellow, but Mute’s gesture is still not identifiable from the report. I should not infer a wire position. Deaf can see the gesture, so I will ask Deaf to describe its physical form in ordinary words—such as which fingers are extended—rather than assigning it a meaning.

```text
speak(to="deaf", text="Please describe Mute's gesture physically, not as a question mark: identify which fingers are extended, whether the thumb is raised, and the hand orientation. Do not infer its manual meaning.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please make one clear, static gesture and hold it. Deaf will describe its physical finger configuration to me.")
```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT orange, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. No new gesture arrived. Mute, please state the exact manual-derived action verbally.

The required wire is still unknown. Mute cannot state it verbally, and the gesture reports contain no identifiable gesture or established code. I will not cut a wire on an inference. Mute must make one of the explicitly defined wire gestures, and Deaf must relay the observed choice in words on the next Deaf turn.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="You cannot speak to me. Make exactly one of these gestures and hold it: thumbs-up means wire 1, victory means wire 2, I-love-you means wire 3. Deaf must report the exact gesture in words.")
```

Deaf says to Blind: Current state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT purple, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute sent one gesture: ?. Its meaning is unknown; do not infer an action from it.

The gesture still cannot be identified, so I will not infer a wire from it. I am switching to a code that does not require recognizing the gesture: Mute should repeat the same gesture a number of times equal to the required wire position. Deaf can report the count in words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use count-only code for the exact manual-required wire: make the same gesture exactly one time for wire 1, two times for wire 2, or three times for wire 3. Deaf, report only how many gestures you see.")
```

Deaf says to Blind: Current state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute sent one gesture: ?. No meaning has been established for it, so do not infer an action yet.

The report confirms only that Mute made one gesture; it does not identify the gesture or establish that Mute followed the proposed counting scheme. Since the manual rule itself remains unverified, cutting wire 1 would still be an unsafe inference. I will request a redundant count signal: Mute should send the required number of gestures twice, and Deaf should report both counts.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not use gesture identity. Encode the manual-required wire by count: send exactly N identical gestures, where N is the required wire position, then repeat the same N-gesture sequence once more. Deaf, report both gesture counts.")
```

No usable manual instruction or reliably decoded signal has arrived. The bomb’s visible state has cycled again, but that does not identify a safe wire, so cutting any position would be an unjustified guess. I will wait rather than detonate the bomb.

```text
wait()
```
